newsitem.title: USA: Control board to reject DC Council budget - paper.
newsitem.headline: Control board to reject DC Council budget - paper.

text.p: The District of Columbia's financial control board plans to reject the D.C. Council's proposed $5.2 billion budget for 1998 on Tuesday, believing it lacks sufficient funding for D.C. public schools and prisons and includes millions of dollars in questionable projected revenue increases, the Washington Post reported on Tuesday.
Board Chairman Andrew Brimmer said the budget requires significant changes before it can be submitted to Congress, the Post reported.
The control board will send the budget back to the D.C. council and the council will have two weeks to look at it. The D.C. budget must be submitted to Congress by mid-June.
Some council members accused the control board members, who were appointed by the president, of substituting their priorities for those of the locally elected officials, the Post reported.
Brimmer said the control board's top priorities are public schools, public safety and public works, the Post reported. ((--U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650))
